01About the community

In briefSoftware professionals and students across the UAE and MENA are welcome, whatever their stack or seniority. Membership is free. The community collects, holds and manages no money.

Policy text · PDF page 1

The UAE | MENA Software Engineers & QA Community is a space for software professionals across the United Arab Emirates and the wider MENA region to connect, learn, and grow together. Members include software engineers, QA specialists, testers, architects, DevOps engineers, product professionals, CEOs, CTOs, and students. Anyone working in or associated with the software engineering industry across the UAE is welcome.

Our aim is to build an environment where all software professionals know each other. Before our community, there were many events across the UAE, but most were promotional programmes rather than initiatives to unite software professionals regardless of tech stack or seniority. That kind of genuine unification was not happening.

This community has existed in the UAE for more than three years. We started with virtual meetups and, with the support of many companies and individuals, have run physical meetups twice a month for the last 1.5 years. We are continuing this mission.

For the past three years, this community has grown through the strong values we uphold and the active support of our members. As the community grows, preserving those values without compromise becomes an even greater responsibility. This document is shared so that every member can understand, protect, and carry those values forward.

Why We Have These Guidelines

As the community grows, more people join, and a bigger crowd needs a shared understanding. These guidelines keep everyone on the same page.

  • Alignment: when every member knows the guidelines, things stay aligned with our community values.
  • Less moderation: when members already know what is expected, community leaders need to step in less often.
  • Saved time: the time leaders save goes back into the community and its initiatives.

Our Five Core Principles

  1. No promotions. This is not a place for selling products, services, or courses, for recruiting, or for self-promotion. It is a place for genuine knowledge exchange.
  2. Unity. We bring together software professionals from every background, nationality, discipline, and experience level across the UAE and MENA as one community.
  3. Safety first. All conversations stay in public community spaces. No unsolicited private messages: this protects everyone from scams, fraud, and harassment.
  4. Quality over quantity. We are not chasing member numbers. We want real, genuine professionals who show up, contribute, and respect the community. Members join only through in-person meetups, not by random invites.
  5. Free and nonprofit. This community will remain free. Community initiatives must serve the community and must not create personal financial gain for any individual. The community does not deal with any finance: there is no membership fee, and no money is collected, held, or managed through the community.
02Joining through a meetup

In briefInvite a friend to an in-person meetup. A moderator adds new members after they attend. Being featured by the community requires explicit consent on the registration form.

Policy text · PDF pages 1–2

New members are added only after attending a community meetup.

This is a deliberate choice. We are not trying to grow a big number. We are trying to build a trusted circle of real software professionals across the UAE and MENA. Anonymous group additions are the fastest way to let in scammers, spammers, and bad actors.

Rules

  1. We do not add random people to the group.
  2. We do not add friends, colleagues, or contacts just to grow the group, even if they are in tech.
  3. New members must attend a community meetup first, in person, so the community can meet them and they can meet the community.
  4. After attending, a moderator will add them to the group.
  5. If you know someone who would be a great fit, invite them to a meetup. Do not give them hope that we add them directly to the group.

Why This Matters

  1. It filters out scammers, spammers, and fake accounts.
  2. It builds real trust: people who have shown up face to face are far less likely to abuse the group.
  3. It keeps the community valued, focused, and high-quality.
  4. It protects existing members from being exposed to unknown contacts.

Meetup Structure

Every community meetup starts with networking. We value the effort members make to attend, often early on Sunday mornings, so the first 30 to 45 minutes are reserved for self-introductions by every attendee and community member. Networking time is never squeezed, so we place it upfront, starting with a warm-up round of self-introductions.

This fulfils our vision of uniting software professionals. After a few meetups, members know each other, can easily coordinate their travel to the venue, and strengthen the overall health of the community and its initiatives.

All attendees who successfully check in at the venue and provide a valid LinkedIn profile link will have their name and LinkedIn profile published in the community announcement area, listed as appreciation for attending the meetup. Featuring is based on each individual’s explicit consent, given through a checkbox on the registration form. Attendees are also often featured on the community LinkedIn page.

03Choosing a WhatsApp group

In briefPost your introduction in Start Here to access the closed groups. Use the directory below to find the right place for a job check, CV review, technical question or event.

Policy text · PDF page 2

Finding your group

Members can use these names to find groups inside the WhatsApp community. For access, contact an admin. New here? Find an in-person meetup ↗.

Start HereJob verificationEngineering & QACV reviewsHR & visasEventsProduct trialsInterview prepOpen sourceHer DubaiOff-topic

Each WhatsApp group has a specific purpose. Use a group only for the purpose described below. The community rules, including the English-only policy, apply in every group.

  1. Start Here: Mandatory Intro. Use this group for mandatory introductions to get access to the other closed groups and maintain the trusted network.
  2. Job Share | Verify | Report Scams & Bad Recruitment Practices. Use this group to share job-related information and verify opportunities. “Verify” means member-led verification: our members are spread across all seven emirates, and some may already work at, or have already interviewed with, the company in question. Their experience and discussion help you verify any opportunity across the UAE. The community does not offer or guarantee jobs, visas, payments, or financial benefits.
  3. Software Engineering & Delivery Discussions Only. Use this group for technical discussions about software engineering, QA, testing, DevOps, and related topics.
  4. Resume/CV + JD Sharing for Review. Use this group for constructive resume reviews and peer feedback.
  5. UAE Job Market | HR | Labour Law | Visa Discussion. Use this group to discuss HR topics and UAE market insights relevant to software professionals. Please note that this group also includes some HR and PRO professionals.
  6. Explore UAE Events, Communities & Networking Opportunities. Use this group to share and explore the UAE community events you attend, and for our own meetup coordination.
  7. Product Trials | Software Repositories | Software & Tooling Catalog. Use this group for relevant product trials and early-access information. Get feedback from community members, or place your product or tool here to get a review.
  8. Learnings | Interview Prep | Experiences & Guidance. Use this group for interview preparation and sharing interview experiences.
  9. Open Source | Discussions, Collaboration & Contributions. Use this group for open-source discussions, projects, and collaboration.
  10. Her Dubai (Ladies Only). A ladies-only group led by women administrators from the community.
  11. Off-Topic | Fun & UAE News Updates. Use this group to share programming memes and verified news, and for anything not covered by the other groups listed above.

Community Contributions

None of our WhatsApp groups has paid actors. All group content comes from community members. Rather than expecting a group to have every piece of information you need, help make the experience fruitful by replying to others, asking questions, and following the community guidelines. Every contribution is a drop in our shared sea of knowledge.

04Leaving and rejoining

In briefYou can leave without explaining why. If you want to return, attend another meetup and follow the same entry process.

Policy text · PDF page 3

This is not a fan page or a group where membership numbers are reported to anyone or any “super boss.” The community has no such expectations of its members. If it is not for you, that is completely fine. You are free to go.

  1. No one will chase you. No DMs asking why you left. No guilt trips. No “please come back.”
  2. No one will block you from returning. If you leave and later want to rejoin, you are welcome to attend another meetup and re-enter through the same process.
  3. No hard feelings. People’s priorities change. Jobs change. Cities change. We understand.
05Language in community spaces

In briefWrite in English so everyone can follow. Clarity matters more than perfect grammar. Give a kind reminder if someone uses another language.

Policy text · PDF page 3

English only in all community spaces, because WhatsApp has no built-in translation feature.

This is not about excluding anyone; it is about including everyone. Our members speak many languages: Arabic, Hindi, Urdu, Malayalam, Tagalog, Russian, French, and more. If we each write in our own language, most people will be left out of the conversation. English is the common language that lets everyone follow, participate, and contribute.

Rules

  1. Write all messages in English.
  2. If English is not your first language, don’t worry. No one will judge your grammar or spelling. Clarity matters more than perfection.
  3. If you see a message in another language, gently remind the person about this rule, kindly and not harshly.
06Private messages and safety

In briefStart conversations publicly. Move to a private message only when both people agree. Selling, recruiting and pitching by DM are prohibited. You can report an unwanted message without replying.

Policy text · PDF page 3

Community discussions happen in public community spaces, so everyone can benefit and moderators can keep the community safe. Private messages are not banned, because professional networking often needs them. What we do not allow is unsolicited and commercial private messages.

Do not send a private (direct) message to a member who has not agreed to it. A conversation that starts publicly can move to private messages once both people agree. This rule exists to protect every member from:

  1. Scams and fraud: fake job offers, crypto schemes, investment pitches, phishing links, fake “opportunities”
  2. Harassment: unwanted attention, pressure, or intimidation
  3. Social engineering: attempts to extract personal, financial, or company information
  4. Impersonation: someone pretending to be a recruiter or employer
  5. Phishing: malicious links sent privately where moderators cannot see them

Rules

  1. No unsolicited private messages. Do not DM a member who has not agreed to it.
  2. No commercial solicitation. Do not use private messages to sell, recruit, promote, or pitch anything.
  3. Private conversations are permitted with mutual consent. For example, following up after a public discussion, sharing a CV with a recruiter, discussing confidential career matters, coordinating a meeting, or exploring a professional collaboration, once both people agree, still with care.
  4. No pressure. Members should never feel pressured to respond or to share personal information. Do not ask members for money, passwords, or OTPs.
  5. Be careful with links and files. Do not click or open links or files from someone you do not know.
  6. You do not have to reply. If someone unknown DMs you from the community, you are not obligated to reply. Report it to the moderators.

If You Receive an Unsolicited DM

  1. Do not click any links or open any files.
  2. Do not share personal, financial, or company information.
  3. Take a screenshot.
  4. Report it to the moderators.

Remember: real opportunities in this community are shared publicly, for everyone. A cold private message offering an opportunity that was never shared publicly is a red flag.

07Promotions and permitted sharing

In briefProhibited promotions lead to immediate removal. Free, relevant resources and verified free UAE events are welcome. Share a tool for genuine technical feedback only in the designated Product Trials group.

Policy text · PDF page 4

To keep this community focused on unity and knowledge-sharing, moderators will not repeatedly delete prohibited content or issue warnings. Posting any of the following will result in immediate removal from the community:

  1. Selling or advertising products, services, paid meetups, or courses
  2. Recruiting posts, job spam, or “DM me for opportunities” messages
  3. Promoting your own profile, blog, YouTube channel, newsletter, or paid content
  4. Referral links, affiliate links, or growth-hacking

What Is Allowed

  1. Sharing free, genuinely useful resources relevant to a discussion
  2. Announcing free community UAE-based events, meetups, or open-source projects (if you are sure the information is valid)
  3. Job discussions (career advice, interview experiences, salary transparency), but not job spam
  4. Sharing a product or tool for genuine technical feedback, only in the designated group “Product Trials | Software Repositories | Software & Tooling Catalog”, provided it does not involve sales pitches, advertising, referral links, or unsolicited marketing

If you are unsure whether something counts as promotion, ask a moderator first.

No Job, Visa, or Financial Guarantees

The community does not offer or guarantee jobs, visas, financial assistance, payments, investments, or any other financial benefit. No one may make such promises in the community.

Partnerships and Sponsorships

All venue partnerships and sponsorships are reviewed by the 10-member admin panel before approval, to ensure they align with our values and do not create inappropriate promotion or affiliation in the community. We will decline or step back from any sponsor that expects aggressive promotion across our network. We may thank and credit venue partners and sponsors, but collaboration does not give permission to market products or services in community spaces. Because the community does not deal with any finance, no sponsorship or partnership involves money being collected, held, or managed by the community or by any individual on its behalf.

08Community values

In briefRespect UAE laws, local culture and fellow members. Welcome newcomers, give people time to reply and discuss disagreements constructively. You can report harassment without confronting the person.

Policy text · PDF pages 4–5

These are the values to which members of the UAE | MENA Software Engineers & QA Community should aspire.

Respect Country Rules & People

Respect the UAE: its laws, its culture, its people. We are guests here. Follow UAE laws and local rules at all times, online and in person. Never involve the community, directly or indirectly, in anything that harms the country, its stability, its reputation, or its social fabric. This is non-negotiable. Violations may result in immediate removal and, where appropriate, referral to the authorities.

Be Friendly and Welcoming

New members, juniors, and people asking “basic” questions are the future of this community. Treat them accordingly.

Be Patient

Do not complain, guilt-trip, or pressure anyone for not responding. Silence is not rejection; it usually just means life is busy. Ask once, wait, and move on. Patience keeps this community healthy.

Be Thoughtful

  1. Productive communication requires effort. Think about how your words will be interpreted across cultures.
  2. Remember that sometimes it is best to refrain entirely from commenting.

Be Respectful

  1. In particular, respect differences of opinion on tools, languages, frameworks, testing approaches, and careers.
  2. Respect differences of nationality, culture, religion, gender, and experience level. Our diversity is our strength.
  3. Show no special bias or preference toward anyone because they work for, or are associated with, a big brand or well-known company. Within the community, everyone is equal.

Be Charitable

  1. Interpret the arguments of others in good faith; do not seek to disagree.
  2. When we do disagree, try to understand why.

Be Constructive

  1. Avoid derailing: stay on topic. If you want to talk about something else, start a new conversation.
  2. Avoid unconstructive criticism: don’t merely decry the current state of affairs; offer, or at least solicit, suggestions as to how things may be improved.
  3. Avoid snarking (pithy, unproductive, sniping comments).
  4. Discussions involving sensitive subjects are permitted when relevant and conducted respectfully. For example, it is fine to discuss workplace discrimination, gender equality, salary inequality, unfair recruitment practices, workplace harassment, or labour law concerns. Personal attacks, discriminatory comments, inflammatory arguments, and harassment are not permitted. For example, insulting someone for their opinion, mocking a person’s nationality, religion, or gender, or repeatedly arguing just to provoke others.
  5. Avoid microaggressions (brief and commonplace verbal, behavioral, and environmental indignities that communicate hostile, derogatory, or negative slights and insults to a person or group).

Be Responsible

What you say and do matters. Take responsibility for your words and actions, including their consequences, whether intended or otherwise.

People are complicated. You should expect to be misunderstood and to misunderstand others; when this inevitably occurs, resist the urge to be defensive or assign blame. Try not to take offense where no offense was intended. Give people the benefit of the doubt. Even if the intent was to provoke, do not rise to it. Everyone should avoid escalating disagreements. However, responsibility for misconduct rests with the person engaging in it. Members experiencing harassment should report it to moderators and are not required to confront the individual.

09Conduct and enforcement

In briefModerators remove members immediately for prohibited promotions, scams, harassment, threats or repeated violations. For a minor first-time mistake, a moderator may give one polite reminder.

Policy text · PDF pages 5–6

9.1 Our Pledge

In the interest of fostering an open and welcoming environment, we as members, contributors, and moderators pledge to make participation in the UAE | MENA Software Engineers & QA Community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size, disability, ethnicity, gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.

9.2 Our Standards

Examples of behavior that contributes to a positive environment include:

  1. Using welcoming and inclusive language
  2. Being respectful of differing viewpoints and experiences
  3. Gracefully accepting constructive criticism
  4. Focusing on what is best for the community
  5. Showing empathy towards other community members
  6. Helping newcomers and answering questions patiently
  7. Sharing knowledge freely and crediting others

Examples of unacceptable behavior include:

  1. The use of sexualized language or imagery and unwelcome sexual attention or advances
  2. Trolling, insulting or derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks
  3. Public or private harassment
  4. Publishing others’ private information, such as a physical or electronic address, without explicit permission
  5. Discriminatory remarks based on nationality, ethnicity, religion, gender, or language
  6. Other conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a professional setting

9.3 Our Responsibilities

Community moderators are responsible for clarifying the standards of acceptable behavior and are expected to take appropriate and fair corrective action in response to any instances of unacceptable behavior.

Community moderators have the right and responsibility to remove messages that are not aligned to this Code of Conduct, or to ban temporarily or permanently any member for other behaviors that they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive, or harmful.

9.4 Conflict Resolution

We do not believe that all conflict is bad; healthy debate and disagreement often yield positive results. However, it is never okay to be disrespectful or to engage in behavior that violates the community’s Code of Conduct.

If you see someone violating the Code of Conduct, you are encouraged to address the behavior directly with community admins. Many issues can be resolved quickly and easily, and this gives people more control over the outcome of their dispute. We are dedicated to providing an environment where participants feel welcome and safe.

9.5 Enforcement

Moderators act quickly and consistently, so the community is not slowed down by repeated warnings.

  1. Message removal. Moderators may remove any message that does not follow these guidelines.
  2. Immediate removal for serious violations. Prohibited promotions (Section 7), scams, and harassment or threatening behaviour result in immediate removal from the community, with no prior warning.
  3. Repeated violations. If a member keeps breaking the community guidelines, we do not spend time on repeated verbal reminders. The member is removed immediately.
  4. First-time minor lapses. For a minor first-time mistake, such as posting in the wrong group or in another language, a moderator may give one polite reminder. The same mistake repeated is treated as a repeated violation.
